diagnosed_root_causes.M2-B28: probe_cgroup_delegation() built its CgroupDelegation inside a try block and removed the probe cgroup in the matching finally, swallowing every OSError. The positive result therefore preceded cleanup in program order and survived its failure, so 'available=true' could coexist with a residual probe cgroup and with the sentence '... was removed'.
diagnosed_root_causes.M2-B29: _topology_is_still_true() re-derived a cached topology from owner PID, directory existence, manager membership, and a basename comparison. A directory removed and recreated under the same name, a parent that regained a process, a controller the kernel stopped offering or distributing, and an unrelated leaf with the same basename all left those four checks green. process_supervision.cgroup_delegation() returned its cached object with no physical check at all once the PID matched.
diagnosed_root_causes.M2-B30: The helper's release op performed the gate write and only then sent a single acknowledgement, and the client raised PrivateWorkspaceError on any non-ok reply or transport failure. An exception therefore covered both 'the write was never attempted' and 'the write completed and the answer was lost'. The caller re-raised immediately with no kill, no reap, no descriptor closure, no cgroup cleanup, and recorded the effect as a process that never started.
diagnosed_root_causes.M2-M31: The report named m2_discovered_total=304 alongside m2_executed=254 without stating that 254 was the pre-B25 legacy subset, and the module list omitted the 50-test B25 module.

protocol_and_state_changes.helper_protocol: The trusted helper's release op now sends RELEASE_ACCEPTED before attempting the gate write and RELEASE_WRITE_COMPLETED or RELEASE_WRITE_FAILED after it. PrivateMountHelper.release() classifies the two frames and returns a GateReleaseOutcome instead of raising, because a raised exception cannot say which side of the write it came from.
